newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Court rules Rosneft owns Purneftegaz.
newsitem.headline: Court rules Rosneft owns Purneftegaz.

text.p: The Moscow regional arbitration court has ruled that Russian oil producer Purneftegaz belongs to state oil holding company Rosneft and not oil group SIDANKO, a lawyer for Rosneft said on Thursday.
"The court upheld the ruling of the first level court, the Moscow city arbitration court, which rejected SIDANKO's claim," Liliya Petrova, deputy head of Rosneft's legal department, said.
SIDANKO could theoretically appeal to the Supreme Arbitration Court, she told Reuters.
But the supreme court has already ruled against SIDANKO in another case brought in the Purneftegaz dispute, she noted.
There was no immediate comment from SIDANKO.
OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (SIDANKO) is one of Russia's largest vertically integrated oil groups.
Its main production units include Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz.
At dispute is a 38 percent stake in OAO Purneftegaz, which covers 51 percent of its voting shares.

SIDANKO claimed that the stake had been allocated to it in 1994 while the Russian government was restructuring the oil industry to build vertically integrated groups. But Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin issued a decree in January 1995 incorporating it in Rosneft.
SIDANKO is mostly owned by Interros-Oil, part of a financial-industrial group built around Uneximbank.
The Russian government intends to privatise Rosneft, but the sale has been delayed by the Purneftegaz dispute.
At 1120 GMT Purneftegaz ordinaries were $3.40 on the Russian Trading System after closing on Thursday at $3.70.
